@cdk-bot please review

> I found a few issues in testing.
> 
> **1. The polling path ignores the marker, so payments are credited twice**
> 
> The push path skips a payment that matches the override marker; the polling path (`check_mint_quote_payments`) doesn't. Live: I overrode 20,000 sat with `--payment-id <txid>:1`, confirmed it, and minted. The wallet got 40,000 sat from one 20,000 sat UTXO.
> 
> **2. A partial `amount` strands BOLT11 quotes**
> 
> `--amount 60` on a 100 sat BOLT11 quote leaves it `PAID` but unmintable, and the real Lightning payment is then ignored. Could reject `amount` on BOLT11 unless it equals the remainder.
> 
> **3. The call can succeed without crediting anything**
> 
> On a 100 sat quote that's already fully paid, `--amount 50` returns OK / `PAID` and credits nothing (`quote.rs:156` returns early). Comments on the rpc conflict with this response, and it's not the best UX.
> 
> **4. Proto changes are breaking changes**
> 
> Changes to the existing rpc should be made in backwards compatible ways. If backwards compatibility is not achievable the breaking service requires a version bump to keep disruptions at the client level minimal.
> 
> **On Scope:** there is an opportunity to split the PR up into different areas of focus. It currently covers rpc logic, core logic, and proto changes.

Thanks for the thorough review and the live reproduction. The polling path deduplication gap is a valid blocker, and the BOLT11 partial override and no op success concerns are also well founded.

I'll address these in the existing PR with focused regression tests. I'll also verify protobuf compatibility and clarify the behavioral changes. I'd prefer to keep the fixes together since they address the same payment accounting correctness issue, while keeping the changes minimal.

A lookback restore can stop before reaching the saved derivation counter. Empty batches within the lookback range count toward `max_gap`, so a sufficiently long unsigned gap causes the scan to terminate even when recoverable proofs exist beyond the original counter.

Could we ensure the scan reaches at least the saved counter before applying normal gap-based termination? This would prevent `resume_restore(Some(lookback))` from recovering less than `resume_restore(None)` solely because of the requested lookback.

When startup encounters a melt saga whose lease is still valid, this branch skips it without scheduling another recovery attempt. Since "Mint::start()" runs reconciliation only once, lease expiry alone does not trigger recovery. The saga can remain pending until another status poll, payment event, or explicit recovery call occurs.

This also affects "SetupComplete" sagas, where no outgoing payment event is expected. Could we schedule a delayed reconciliation after lease expiry, with ownership checked again before processing?
This PR is stale because it has been open for 60 days with no activity.

Related: #2720 tracks loss of structured error categories/source context through FFI, confirmed in 0.18.2 and main `87c2bf976ffca162c9023e21615398d3aa94ee52`.

Keeping recovery semantics here rather than opening a duplicate: richer transport errors cannot establish whether a dispatched payment settled or compensation completed. The wallet needs a typed recovery outcome for those decisions, separately from accurate recipient-versus-mint error messages. Both efforts should coordinate with #2479.

> Could we keep this focused on the outstanding-quote contract? The documentation updates and tests for existing-quote execution and recovery address #2637. The in-flight test adds a separate timing guarantee and substantial backend scaffolding; I'd consider separating it and reusing existing helpers for the remaining tests. Please also drop the unrelated `cdk-bdk` formatting change.
> 
> The CLI/RPC and mint API documentation should explicitly state the intended contract: disabling melting stops creation of new melt quotes; previously issued, otherwise valid quotes remain executable; already-dispatched payments continue through normal recovery and reconciliation. No production logic change is needed for that contract.
> 
> Please avoid promising that every in-flight quote request is rejected. A request that has already passed the disabled-state check can still complete, so any wording retained should describe that acceptance-check boundary.

Done, please review 
NB: the contract is clear now and ready to merge

I'll take this one. I'll focus on correcting the receive recovery state transitions so tokens spent elsewhere cannot be marked as completed, while preserving legitimate recovery after a lost mint response. I'll add regression coverage for both cases.

Closing as already included in v0.18.2 via commit 322fe0b09c8c634497ef3fdf3c41b69830105cfd. I verified that this commit is in the v0.18.2 release history and its file tree is identical to this PR’s head (4795170dea627917c5c5830b85e1ea6251ba87f7). The release notes also list the mint quote signing-key recovery feature: https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/releases/tag/v0.18.2

This appears to address the same underlying recipient-fee underfunding issue as #2499 (which references #2493), though the approaches differ: #2499 targets an exact recipient amount after redemption fees, while this PR permits denomination surplus for payment requests while preserving explicit exact-send guarantees, and covers broader accounting and recovery paths.

I have not reviewed which approach is better or whether either fully supersedes the other. Flagging the overlap so the two fixes can be compared and reconciled before merging.
